title: ～たものだ — nostalgic “used to ～”
summary: Verb ta-form + ものだ recalls a habit or a scene of the past with a feeling of nostalgia: “I used to ～.” Often paired with よく, 昔, 子どもの頃. It is used only for things that no longer happen.

patterns.gloss: ta-form + ものだ (泳いだものだ, 話したものだ)

patterns.form: 動詞ていた ＋ ものだ
patterns.gloss: te-ita form for a state that continued (広がっていたものだ)

body.p: The ta-form states the past event, and ものだ adds the speaker's feeling of looking back fondly. 子どもの頃、よく泳いだものだ means “I swam so often back then (and I miss it).” It attaches to the plain past form of a verb.
Use it to tell memories of your childhood, school days or an old town. The habit has ended, so it is not used for the present or for a single event.
～ていた just describes a past habit or state. ～たものだ also expresses nostalgia. Adding よく, 昔 or 頃 makes the sentence sound natural.

examples.ja: 子（こ）どもの頃（ころ）、よくこの川（かわ）で泳（およ）いだものだ。
examples.romaji: Kodomo no koro, yoku kono kawa de oyoida mono da.
examples.tr: When I was a child, I used to swim in this river often.

examples.ja: 学生（がくせい）の頃（ころ）は、友（とも）だちと朝（あさ）まで話（はな）したものだ。
examples.romaji: Gakusei no koro wa, tomodachi to asa made hanashita mono da.
examples.tr: Back in my student days, I used to talk with friends until morning.

examples.ja: 昔（むかし）は、この辺（あた）りにも広（ひろ）い畑（はたけ）が広（ひろ）がっていたものだ。
examples.romaji: Mukashi wa, kono atari ni mo hiroi hatake ga hirogatte ita mono da.
examples.tr: Long ago, wide fields used to spread out around here too.
examples.note: ていた + ものだ recalls a scene that is now gone.

pitfalls: It is only for past habits that have ended. Do not use it for a one-time event or something still happening.
Do not confuse it with a general-truth ～ものだ (as in 子どもは遊ぶものだ). Here it follows the ta-form and is nostalgic.
